newsitem.title: USA: CBOT members mull changes to night financial trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT members mull changes to night financial trade.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade members met Monday to discuss several alternatives to night open outcry sessions in financial markets, including extending the daytime pit session, exchange sources said.

Three options under consideration were: extending daytime open outcry to 1500 or 1530 CDT (2000 or 2030 GMT) from the current 1400 CDT (1900 GMT) close, moving up the night open outcry session to late afternoon, and replacing the night session altogether with the Project A electronic system.
If CBOT directors recommend restructuring the trading day at their Wednesday board meeting, a membership vote will follow in mid-May.
Monday's meeting was the final forum for discussing the thorny issue of the night session's fate.

"It was well attended, with a good deal of give and take by those in favor of closing the evening session and those who were equally outspoken on the other side," said David Prosperi, CBOT senior vice president.

CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor said in a letter to members last week the exchange must decide how to best position itself for the 24-hour trading day. "We must make a strategic decision based on facts, not emotions," he wrote.

The issue is contentious because big brokerage firms are in favor of scrapping night open outcry due to cost, while locals and younger traders see it as a stepping stone and a source of supplemental income.
However, trading volume in the night pit session has been declining steadily while Project A has been enjoying healthy growth.
Details of the three proposals circulated to members follow:
-- Expand the daytime pit session to close at 1500 or 1530 CDT (2000 or 2030 GMT), followed by Project A from 1630 to 0645 CDT (2130 to 1145 GMT).
-- Shift evening open outcry to 1500-1700 CDT (2000-2200 GMT), followed by Project A from 1730 to 0645 (2230 to 1145 GMT).
-- Scrapping the night pit session in favor of Project A sessions from 1430-1630 CDT (1930-2130 GMT) and 1730-0645 CDT (2230-1145 GMT).
Current daytime pit hours are 0720 to 1400 CDT (1230 to 1900 GMT), followed by Project A afternoon session, night pit trading, and the overnight Project A session.
If members vote to end night open outcry, the exchange said it would target August 28 as the date of the final session.
